subject: Dedicated inference recap & next steps — Acme Robotics
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Dedicated inference needs & capacity targets — Redwood / Acme Robotics

Hi Liam — thanks again for the time today. Below is a succinct recap from our call so we’re aligned and can move to a technical deep dive and MPA. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points and goals
- Current on-prem GPUS are oversubscribed during nightly batch runs; inconsistent p95 latency for interactive ops (~400–600ms).
- Need a predictable, reserved inference tier for customer-facing features (control plane + data isolation).
- Compliance: SOC 2 scope and US data residency required.
- Goal: move critical inference paths to a dedicated pool with predictable latency and clear costing.

Key requirements we captured
- Capacity: target baseline of 8 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs (able to sustain ~120 concurrent streams at 512-token profiles) with 2x burst headroom for peaks.
- Isolation: VPC/private deployment option, customer-managed network peering, KMS for key management.
- Scaling: autoscale policy to add burst nodes when queue depth > 50 for > 2m; warm cache priming for predictable p95.
- SLA targets: target 99.9% monthly uptime; latency goal p95 ≤ 150ms for 512-token requests on warm nodes (we discussed 150–200ms range — aiming low).
- Timeline: PoC environment in a 2–4 week window, production reserved start target by mid-November (subject to procurement).

Immediate next steps (owner in parentheses)
1) I’ll share an MPA + pricing PDF and a SOC2 evidence intake checklist (Vanessa) — attached.
2) Schedule a 60-min tech deep dive to validate network, deployment, and autoscaling configuration (Marcus).
3) Your team to confirm procurement timeline and any internal PO requirements (Liam / Procurement).
4) Rishi to prepare a short network isolation diagram and sample config for private deployment.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-ACME.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep dive.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive\Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0120

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2025 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Tech deep dive scheduling + infra notes

Hi all — following Vanessa’s thread: thanks for penciling us in. Confirming Wed, Oct 8, 09:30–10:30 ET for the deep dive. I’ll cover autoscaling, burst capacity, and a recommended SLA/fallback plan. A few technical notes to prep the call: 

1) Baseline vs burst: the 8-GPU reserved pool gives predictable warm-cache latency. Burst nodes should be configured as preemptible instances with fast cold-start paths and a 2-minute priming window. We recommend a headroom policy of +25% burst for short spikes; longer sustained increases should trigger scaling of the reserved pool in coordination with you.

2) SLA framing: we typically support 99.9% monthly uptime on reserved pools; for 99.95% we’ll need a two-region active/passive setup and a capacity commitment increase. For latency, warm-node p95 ≤ 150ms (512 tokens) is achievable in our bench; cold-start p95 will be higher — we’ll show actual numbers during the demo.

3) Security & isolation: expect an architecture with VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, and audit log delivery to your Splunk/ELK endpoint. Rishi will attach a one-page diagram in the morning.

4) PoC window: recommend a 4-week PoC with telemetry enabled (latency, token-cost, cache hit rates). We’ll provide: simple SLO dashboard, per-route cost breakdown, and an ops playbook for fallbacks.

Attachment: infra-sketch.png (PNG, 22KB)
DocuSign (optional MOU): https://docusign.example.com/rooms/ACME-MOU-9876

See you on the call — Marcus
